Sara: quick heads-up — new profiling run on continuous-batching + multimodel routing shows unexpected tail latency when fallback kicks in :thinking_face:
Ben: can you paste the top-line numbers?
Sara: baseline steady-state p95 ~ 85ms. With routing->fallback to compat-variant, p95 jumps to 180-240ms for short prompts (<=32 tokens). p50 still ~90ms.
Max: that smells like batching starvation or expensive kernel path for the fallback variant. did the run include kernel selection changes?
Sara: yes. we rolled the kernel patch that prefers fused-attn kernels for 1..64 seq. But fallback variants are quantized and hit a different kernel path leading to longer per-token latency. profiler shows lots of small batches (1-3) on fallback lanes.
Priya: interesting — so two things: (A) kernel mismatch causing slower per-token throughput, and (B) batch formation different because compat set filtering increases heterogeneity.
Nora: do we have KV cache metrics? if fallback triggers full reencode or cache miss, that'd explain the spike for short tokens.
Sara: KV cache stats attached from run:
```
kv_hits: 72.4%
kv_misses: 27.6%
avg_kv_miss_penalty_ms: 96.3
batch_size_dist: {1: 21%, 2: 31%, 3: 20%, 4+: 28%}
```
Ben: 27% miss rate is higher than usual. Might be because fallback variants don't share cache keys with primary variant (different quant/format).
Max: exactly — our compatibility sets currently treat variants as compatible for routing, but not for cache key equivalence. So when user falls back from fp16->int8, KV keys are invalidated.
Priya: any logs showing queue wait times?
Sara: yes — queue latency histogram: many requests spend ~12-18ms in queue but some singletons get dispatched immediately while waiting for compat checks. That creates uneven batching.
infra-bot: deploy:continuous-batching/2024-11-02 by @deploy-bot — rolled kernel-selection patch to canary (3 nodes) at 21:07 UTC
Nora: can you share the batch formation pseudocode we used? I want to see where compat filtering runs.
Sara: snippet from runtime: 
```
# accept reqs into queue
while True:
  req = queue.pop()
  compat = compat_set_for(req.model, req.variant)
  candidates = find_compatible_waiting(compat, token_budget_remaining)
  batch = select_batch(candidates, max_tokens)
  dispatch(batch)
```
Ben: we run compat_set_for early, which filters queued requests before considering them for batching. That seems to fragment batches when many requests are only compatible with fallback variants.
Max: hypothesis: moving compat-set checks later (after forming a larger token-aware batch) and then splitting into kernel-homogeneous sub-batches might increase batching density. But need to ensure latency SLO for compatible immediate dispatch.
Priya: also evaluate relaxing token_budget targets for short prompts. Right now max_tokens_per_batch is tuned for 128 token avg; for <=32 prompts it's suboptimal.
Sara: ran a synthetic with delayed-compat check: form provisional batch by arrival time up to 12ms or 256 token budget, then group by kernel path. result: p95 for fallback cases dropped from 200ms -> 120ms, p50 unchanged. kv_miss unchanged though.
Nora: so two levers: batching policy reorder, and KV cache equivalence across variants. Which is lower risk?
Max: batching reorder is lower infra risk. Changing cache key semantics is risky (security/consistency). But we can add a KV translation layer that maps compatible variants to canonical keys safely for same-model semantics. That requires careful correctness checks.
Ben: can we do interim: aggressive batching when queue depth low, but only statically limit reordering window (e.g., 8-12ms)? That should reduce singleton dispatches and improve packing for fallbacks.
Priya: yes — also consider dynamic token budget that lowers per-batch token cap when many short prompts are present, but raises it for heterogenous variant loads.
Sara: action items I propose:
- Max: prototype delayed-compat batching (bring compat check after provisional batch) and bench (A)
- Nora: investigate feasibility and correctness constraints for canonical KV mapping across variants (B)
- Ben: tune token_budget thresholds for short prompts and add metric dashboards for batch fragmentation (C)
- Priya: run additional AB tests on canary nodes with reverted kernel and current kernel to isolate kernel path penalty (D)
Nora: +1 on dashboards. we'll need metrics: batch_fragmentation_ratio, compat_hit_rate, kv_miss_by_variant, per-kernel p95.
Max: I'll start on (A) today. Expect initial bench by EOD tomorrow.
Sara: posting profiler traces and the raw run id: run-2024-11-02-1749 in #artifacts. Please annotate if you see something else.
Ben: quick note — if we add delayed compat, ensure we don't block high-priority routes (enterprise-tier). Might need route-level policy to opt-out.
Priya: good call. add route.allow_reorder boolean to config.
Nora: ok, I'll add dashboards and a gating experiment plan.
Sara: thanks team. small follow-up: observed a few OOMs on the canary nodes when we increased provisional batch token cap to 512 during synthetic. keep that in mind.
Max: noted — I'll include an OOM safety bound in the prototype.
Sara: cool. ping me if you want the profiler snippet. :thumbsup:
